title: Aldol addition: enolate + aldehyde → β-hydroxy aldehyde
why: Hydroxide removes an α-H to make an enolate. Its α-carbon then runs pattern A on a second aldehyde: nucleophilic addition to the C=O carbon. Protonating the alkoxide gives a β-hydroxy aldehyde.

traps.explains: That's the aldol condensation product. Losing water to form the C=C needs heat; at low temperature the reaction stops at the β-hydroxy aldehyde.
The new C–C bond joins the α-carbon of one aldehyde to the carbonyl carbon of the other, so the OH ends up on the β-carbon, not the α-carbon.
Hydroxide isn't a reducing agent. The aldehyde C=O survives; only the attacked C=O becomes an alcohol.

review: Check the conditions (NaOH, 5 °C = addition; heat = condensation) follow the usual textbook split.
